game.name: Ziibiing
game.description: New in 0.8.83: the year now turns the stories too - the sugar bush opens when the sap runs and the ricing when the rice ripens, and out of their season the old errands wait for you. Ma'iingan shows you a nagwaagan (snare) and asks for a hare. Migizi builds a jiimaan (birch bark canoe) for you at the landing, which takes him two days of work. You can lay asemaa (tobacco) or apaakozigan on the flames of a village fire and give thanks before you take anything from the land, and the ground there is blessed for you that day. Along the still water grows miskwaabiimizh (red willow): peel its bark and mix it with asemaa at any fire to make apaakozigan of your own. The interface now wears the village's own smoked hide with a beadwork edge and the village's own marks for every skill, and a child born here stands in village clothes from the first moment. New: first stories by the river - Mishoomis shows you how to make fire with flint, Mitigwaabiike the bow maker teaches you to make a maple bow and birch arrows and gives you a tomahawk, Ma'iingan takes you on a deer hunt for sinew, and obsidian from the riverbank makes the best arrowheads. Your bow is bound to you: it can never be lost, sold or traded. New: the village now has no gold - you begin with only what you carry. To the north an old forest of great pines and cedars, too thick to walk through and too old to cut, shelters the river valley. Ziibiing means "at the river". Begin a new life in an Anishinaabe village of birch bark wigwams on a wide river. You wake by the fire in your mother's wigwam: choose who you are - man or woman, long hair, braids or a mohawk, a ribbon shirt, a beaded vest or buckskin, a ribbon skirt or a breechcloth, and moccasins. Ningashi, your mother, sees to your hair and clothes, and Mishoomis, the grandfather of the village, waits in his own lodge. The people of Ziibiing each know their part of the world - the canoe, the fish, the wild rice, the plants and birds, the moon, the weather, the sun and stars - and they speak to you as one of their own. Paddle a jiimaan (birch bark canoe) down the river, go ricing with a friend in the ricing moon, peel wiigwaas (birch bark), tap the maples in the spring sap run and boil the sap into syrup and candy for Nookomis. The year turns through the seasons on a whole planet you can walk, paddle or fly across, shared with everyone else who plays. Your character keeps its own bag and save, and the birch bark makak by the village fire holds everything in your arcade wallet. Dance regalia is earned, not given. Solo or online.
